metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in El Moro, CO | Raton Basin CBM
metaDescription: Own coalbed methane minerals near El Moro, Las Animas County? We buy Raton Basin interests directly, priced off your actual decline curve.
heroLead: El Moro sits just north of Trinidad in the Colorado portion of the Raton Basin, a coalbed methane field that has quietly produced gas from the Vermejo and Raton formations since the 1990s.
intro: Las Animas County mineral ownership around El Moro often traces back to coal mining and ranching land where the mineral estate has been passed through a family for well over a century, sometimes with coal rights and oil and gas rights held separately from one another.

Raton Basin wells are lower-volume, longer-life producers compared to the Wattenberg core up north, and many El Moro-area tracts have been under lease and paying modest but steady royalties for years.

sections.heading: How Raton Basin CBM differs from DJ Basin shale
paragraphs: Coalbed methane wells here produce water first as the coal seam depressurizes, with gas volumes building over time and then declining gradually over a long well life. This is a much different curve than a fast-declining horizontal shale well, and it means older El Moro interests can still carry real value.

sections.heading: Coal and mineral rights can be split
paragraphs: Because this area has a coal mining history, some deeds separate coal rights from oil and gas rights entirely. Before we price an interest, we confirm exactly what your deed conveys, since an offer on oil and gas minerals is not the same transaction as a coal rights sale.

sections.heading: Verifying title through Las Animas County
paragraphs: We pull recorded leases, unit agreements, and prior conveyances through the Las Animas County Clerk and Recorder to confirm your net revenue interest. Older Raton Basin chains of title can involve several transfers over the decades, so this step takes a bit more time here than in a newer DJ Basin unit.

faqs.question: What is coalbed methane and why does it matter for value?
faqs.answer: It is natural gas trapped in coal seams that produces water early and gas later, with a long, gradual decline. It supports a longer value tail than a fast-declining shale well.

faqs.question: Does my deed include both coal and oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not always. We review your deed specifically to confirm what mineral rights you actually hold before pricing an offer.

faqs.question: How long have Raton Basin wells near El Moro been producing?
faqs.answer: Many wells in this field have been online since the 1990s, giving us a long production history to price your interest against.

faqs.question: Is the title work slower for this area?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, since older Las Animas County chains of title can involve more historical transfers than newer DJ Basin units.
